title: standardize-api-rate-limit-idempotency-retry-after-streaming-openai-compat
author: Asha Raman
description: Motivation: Improve API robustness around rate limiting, idempotency, and streaming stability while keeping OpenAI-compat behavior predictable for SDKs. This PR standardizes HTTP rate-limit headers and JSON error payloads, extends idempotency semantics to streaming and function/tool-calling flows, and adds a clear 'retry_after' surface for mid-stream interruptions. Key goals: 1) Consistent 4xx/5xx error schemas (OpenAI-compat error object), 2) Stable streaming termination semantics with a final error frame and explicit retry_after value when applicable, 3) Idempotency support for streaming/tool-call requests including deduplication + TTL, 4) Backward-compatible headers: always include Retry-After (seconds) when 429 or transient 503 occurs, and 5) Update SDKs and docs with migration notes. Changes are incremental and guarded behind a feature flag (api.robustness.v1) to allow rollout. Checklist: [x] Server-side header and payload changes implemented, [x] Streaming protocol frames extended with final-error metadata, [x] Idempotency store + eviction/TTL added, [x] Unit and integration tests added, [x] Python and TS SDKs updated to honor Retry-After headers and idempotency for streaming, [x] Docs and migration notes updated. Related Linear issues: ENG-4218, ENG-4350. Related incident: SUP-1183 (rate-limit spike during holiday release). Migration notes: SDKs will now surface a structured error object {"type","message","code","params"} for compatibility; clients should inspect error.code and Retry-After headers for automated retries. Rolling strategy: enable flag on staging, smoke test with high-concurrency replay, then staggered rollout to production regions with monitoring (metrics: api.rate_limit.* and streaming.final_error.*).
commits: add: standardize Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* semantics across API gateway and runtime
feat(streaming): append final error frame with structured error + retry_after when mid-stream rate-limited
feat(idempotency): extend idempotency-key handling to streaming and function calls; add dedupe store with TTL and response-hash
chore(sdk): python/ts SDKs: surface retry_after header and propagate idempotency for stream requests
test: add integration tests for mid-stream 429 semantics and idempotent replays
docs: update openai-compat migration guide and troubleshooting for rate limits

redwood/runtime/idempotency.py - new dedupe store interface + TTL and response hash
redwood/openai_compat/errors.py - unified error object and mapping from internal errors
redwood/observability/metrics.py - add api.rate_limit.* and streaming.final_error.* metrics
redwood-sdk-python/redwood/streaming.py - honor Retry-After and idempotency for streaming endpoints

review_comments: Diego: Can we avoid unbounded growth of the idempotency store? What eviction policy and metrics are in place?

Asha: We added a TTL default 24h and an LRU eviction backed by Redis maxmemory LRU with explicit metrics (idempotency.store.size and idempotency.evictions). Added a migration note that very high QPS customers can opt into external dedupe store.
Lina: Concern about SDK behavior when a stream is terminated mid-response with 429 - will SDK surface the final frame and allow deterministic retry?
Asha: SDKs now expose a StreamError event that includes the structured error and retry_after; we've added a deterministic 'replay' helper that reuses the same idempotency-key for safe retries.
release_notes: Server: standardizes rate-limit headers (Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Remaining/Reset) and returns a consistent OpenAI-compatible error object for 4xx/5xx errors. Streaming: when a stream is interrupted by transient rate limiting the server emits a final error frame including a retry_after value. Idempotency: idempotency-keys are now supported for streaming and function/tool calls; dedupe store with TTL prevents duplicate side-effects. SDKs: Python/TS clients updated to honor Retry-After and surface structured stream errors. Backwards-compatible behind feature flag.
notes: Performance: microbenchmarks show <2% median latency regression on normal traffic because of header additions; batching unchanged
Metrics: new dashboards added for api.rate_limit.exceeded and streaming.final_error.rate
Rollout plan: feature flag gating, staged rollout by region, watch idempotency.store.size and api.rate_limit.* metrics
